subject: general
question: Identify the type of cell that is long and branched.
solution:
The correct solution is __**Nerve cell.**__

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• Nerve cells, or neurons, are fundamental components of the **nervous system**.
 
• It transmits electrical impulses and facilitates communication within the body.
 
• Nerve cells, or neurons, have a distinctive structure with a cell body,
 
 
• **Dendrites **(which receive signals), and
 
• **Axon** (which transmits signals). 
 
 
 
• **Neurotransmitters**, chemical messengers, are released at the synapses (junctions) between neurons—to transmit signals from one neuron to another.
 
• Nerve cells have various functions, including sensory processing, motor control, cognitive functions like memory and learning, and regulating bodily functions like heart rate and digestion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__ **

 
• Blood cells are essential components of the **circulatory system**, responsible for various functions crucial to maintaining health and well-being.
 
• There are three main types of blood cells:
 
 
• **Red blood cells (erythrocytes), **
 
• **White blood cells (leukocytes), and **
 
• **Platelets (thrombocytes).** 
 
 
 
• **Red Blood Cells (RBCs):** Red blood cells are responsible for carrying oxygen from the lungs to tissues throughout the body and transporting carbon dioxide back to the lungs for exhalation. They contain **hemoglobin**,a protein that binds to oxygen molecules.
 
• **White Blood Cells (WBCs):** White blood cells are part of the immune system and play a crucial role in defending the body **against infections** and foreign invaders. 
 
• **Platelets:** Platelets are small cell fragments involved in **blood clotting (coagulation)**. When a blood vessel is injured, platelets adhere to the site of injury and release clotting factors to form a blood clot, which helps prevent excessive bleeding. Platelets also participate in wound healing and tissue repair processes.
